author: regime
note: Regime predicates 77-84, 93-94. bars[0] is the reference (newest closed) bar; index increases going back in time. Trend-strength/RANGING windows read bars 0..9; the 11th bar (index10) is inert filler. HIGH_VOL_REGIME and REGIME_TRANSITION use flat doji rangebars whose true range equals the stated span. See suspected_defects for the band overlap/gap findings.

fixtures.rationale: A strong up regime is a run where almost every bar closes up and price is net higher: all 10 bars bullish and close[0]=105 far above close[9]=100.5.
Only 3 of 10 bars close up even though price drifts higher; a market that is up on a minority of bars is not a strong uptrend, so this must not fire.

All 10 bars close above their own open yet each bar gaps lower so close[0]=100 sits BELOW close[9]=104.5: net direction is down, not a strong uptrend. This also shows the band leaves a gap (10 bulls but net-down fires nothing).
bulls=7 sits just inside the bulls>=7 floor and close[0]>close[9] holds, so the predicate fires. Integer count, so inside means exactly at the floor.
One fewer bull than the inside case: bulls=6 is below the bulls>=7 floor, so UP_STRONG does not fire even though price is still net up.
A weak up regime is a mild bullish majority: 6 of 10 bars close up, more than half but far from a dominant trend.
8 of 10 bars close up: that is a dominant, strong bull majority, not a weak one, so the weak band must not claim it.
Only 3 of 10 bars close up: bears are the majority, so this is not any kind of up regime and the weak-up band must not fire.
bulls=5 is just inside the [5,6] band's lower edge, so UP_WEAK fires. NOTE: this SAME 5-bull/5-bear window also fires DOWN_WEAK (bears=5 within [5,6]) - the two bands overlap at a balanced count.
bulls=4 is one below the band's lower edge and thus outside [5,6]; UP_WEAK does not fire.
bulls=6 sits on the inside of the band's upper edge (<=6), so UP_WEAK fires. Distinct bar arrangement from the positive case.
bulls=7 is one above the band's upper edge (>6), so it lies outside [5,6] and UP_WEAK does not fire (UP_STRONG territory instead).
Ranging means price oscillates and closes near the middle of its recent band. Over 10 bars hi=110 lo=100 mid=105; close[0]=105.0 sits dead on the midpoint.
close[0]=109.8 is pinned near the top of the 100-110 band (|109.8-105|=4.8, way past 25% of the 10-point span). Price at the range high is a breakout posture, not ranging.
close[0]=100.6 is pinned near the bottom of the band (|100.6-105|=4.4, well past 25% of the 10-point span). Price at the range low is breakdown posture, not ranging.
span=10, 25% of span=2.5. close[0]=107.3 gives |107.3-105|=2.3, inside the 0.25*span cutoff (2.3<2.5) so RANGING fires.
Same band, close[0]=107.7 gives |107.7-105|=2.7, outside the 0.25*span cutoff (2.7>2.5) so RANGING does not fire. Bar0 high 107.9 keeps hi=110 unchanged.
A weak down regime is a mild bearish majority: 6 of 10 bars close down (bulls=4), more than half but not a dominant downtrend.
8 of 10 bars close down (bulls=2): a dominant, strong bear majority, not a weak one, so the weak-down band must not claim it.
7 of 10 bars close up (bears=3): the market is up on a majority of bars, so a down regime of any strength must not fire.
bears=5 is just inside the [5,6] band, so DOWN_WEAK fires. This is the SAME balanced 5-bull/5-bear window used for UP_WEAK's inside case: both weak bands fire together - an overlap.
bears=4 (bulls=6) is one below the band's lower edge and outside [5,6], so DOWN_WEAK does not fire.
bears=6 (bulls=4) sits on the inside of the band's upper edge (<=6), so DOWN_WEAK fires. Distinct arrangement from the positive case.
bears=7 (bulls=3) is above the band's upper edge (>6), outside [5,6], so DOWN_WEAK does not fire (DOWN_STRONG territory).
A strong down regime is a run where almost every bar closes down and price is net lower: 8 of 10 bars bearish and close[0]=100 well below close[9]=104.5.
Only 6 of 10 bars close down (bears=6) though price is net lower; a minority-dominated slide is at most a weak downtrend, not a strong one.
8 of 10 bars close down yet each bar gaps higher so close[0]=105 sits ABOVE close[9]=100.5: net direction is up, not a strong downtrend. Shows the close test can veto a heavy bear count (a band gap).
bears=7 sits just inside the bears>=7 floor and close[0]<close[9], so the predicate fires.
One fewer bear than the inside case: bears=6 is below the bears>=7 floor, so DOWN_STRONG does not fire though price is still net down.
A high-vol regime is a bar whose range dwarfs recent volatility. 20 prior bars each span 1.0 (atr20=1.0); the reference bar spans 3.0 = 3x atr, a clear spike.
The reference bar spans 1.0, identical to the 20 prior bars (atr20=1.0). A bar in line with recent range is normal volatility, not a spike.

Every bar, including the reference, spans 3.0 so atr20=3.0. Volatility is high in absolute terms but the reference bar is NOT elevated relative to it (3.0 < 2*3.0). Regime is about a relative spike, so this must not fire.
atr20=1.0; reference range 2.2 is above the 2.0*atr cutoff (2.2>2.0), inside the firing region.
atr20=1.0; reference range 1.8 is below the 2.0*atr cutoff (1.8<2.0), outside the firing region.

A regime transition is volatility expanding fast: the last 5 bars each span 3.0 while the 20-bar backdrop averages ~1.5 (atr5=3.0, atr20=1.5, ratio 2.0). Short-term vol has jumped well above the long-term baseline.
Every bar spans 1.0 so atr5=atr20=1.0 (ratio 1.0). A steady, unchanging volatility level is the opposite of a transition.
Recent 5 bars span 1.0 while the older backdrop spans 3.0: atr5=1.0, atr20=2.5, ratio 0.4. Volatility is CONTRACTING, not expanding, so a transition-to-high-vol reading is wrong.
Recent 5 bars span 2.0 over a range-1.0 backdrop: atr5=2.0, atr20=(5*2+15*1)/20=1.25, ratio 1.6 is above the 1.5 cutoff (inside firing region).
Recent 5 bars span 1.6 over a range-1.0 backdrop: atr5=1.6, atr20=(5*1.6+15)/20=1.15, ratio 1.39 is below the 1.5 cutoff (outside firing region).

Price advanced (close[4]=100 up to close[2]=106) then the latest bar barely moves: |close0-close1|=0.2 is tiny next to the early thrust |close3-close4|=4 (0.2 < 0.3*4=1.2). Momentum has stalled after a rise: exhaustion.
There is no prior advance to exhaust: close[4]=106 is ABOVE close[2]=100, so price fell over that span. The up-move precondition fails and this must not fire.
The advance is real (close[4]=100 below close[2]=106) but the latest bar moves hard: |close0-close1|=3.0 is larger than the early thrust's 30% (0.3*4=1.2). Momentum is intact, not exhausted.
Early thrust |close3-close4|=4 so cutoff=0.3*4=1.2. Latest move |close0-close1|=1.0 is under the cutoff (1.0<1.2), inside the firing region.
Same early thrust and cutoff 1.2, but latest move |close0-close1|=1.4 is over the cutoff (1.4>1.2), outside the firing region.
High efficiency means net move ~ total path: a straight 100->110 climb one point per bar has net=10 and path=10, er=1.0. Every step of travel counted.
Price oscillates 100<->102 and ends where it began: net=0 over path=20, er=0. Maximum back-and-forth, zero efficiency, must not read as high.
Net move 4 over a wandering path of 10 gives er=0.4: a middling, choppy advance, well short of an efficient trend.
net=8, path=10 gives er=0.8, above the 0.7 cutoff (inside firing region).
net=6, path=10 gives er=0.6, below the 0.7 cutoff (outside firing region).
Low efficiency means much travel, little net progress: 100<->102 oscillation ends flat, net=0 over path=20, er=0. Textbook inefficient/choppy market.
A straight 100->110 climb has net=path=10, er=1.0: perfectly efficient trending, the opposite of low efficiency.
Net move 4 over path 10 gives er=0.4: middling efficiency, above the low threshold, so not an inefficient/choppy regime.
net=2, path=8 gives er=0.25, below the 0.3 cutoff (inside the low-efficiency firing region).
net=3, path=9 gives er=0.333, above the 0.3 cutoff (outside the low-efficiency firing region).
